intro.text: Allomancer Jak, also called Gentleman Jak: a nobleman and celebrated explorer whose adventures appear in the broadsheets.
An adventurer who, like Wax, started out collecting bounties in the Roughs, about six years before him. Wax finds his stories ridiculous and calls him a fop rather than a real lawman.

Allomancer Jak, or Gentleman Jak: a nobleman and explorer whose adventures fill the broadsheets. He began hunting bounties in the Roughs some years before Wax, who finds his stories ridiculous and calls him a fop.
Allomancer Jak, or Gentleman Jak: a nobleman and explorer whose widely read broadsheet adventures now claim Wax as his old comrade.

items.text: In the Roughs, Jak saved Handerwym from drowning in a lake, and Handerwym became his companion and assistant, correcting his accounts and adding biting notes. His travels took him to ever more distant and dangerous places: in one tale he was flung into the sea bound to a bust of the Survivor, and he has been taken captive many times and knocked on the head no fewer than eighteen times.

In the Pits of Eltania, Jak shot a koloss who challenged him, part of a plan to win the tribe's acceptance that Handerwym thought foolish. Then, trapped in a canyon cave, he burned tin from the rock, met his guide Lyndip, and escaped by riding a flooding river. Recaptured, he declared himself a koloss and proved it by diving into a lake for the Survivor's Treasure: an aluminum box of spikes.

Jak kept publishing his adventures and stumbled on a great many Survivor artifacts. He also warmed to Wax, writing him into his tales as an old comrade; Wax denies it, but plays along when it helps comfort someone or get information.

appearance.text: His broadsheets show a well-groomed man in his early thirties with a big mustache, long hair and glasses, usually in a suit with a mistcloak, and a cowboy hat when out exploring.

personality.text: In his own tales Jak is clever, bold and unflappable, escaping every danger by his wits, and he rates honesty as his greatest virtue. Handerwym's notes tell another story: a careless man who rarely checks his facts, misreads situations and tends to make them worse.
